expectations.text: Lays out a quarterly rhythm: Q1 scoping refresh/RCM updates, Q2 walkthroughs + interim testing, Q3 second testing wave + deficiency triage while remediation windows remain, Q4 roll-forward/update testing, remediation validation, aggregation analysis, management's 404(a) conclusion
expectations.evidence: Q1 "Refresh the risk assessment and scoping... update the RCM... Kick off Q1 walkthroughs"; Q2 heaviest interim testing; Q3 "'remediation deadline' quarter... classify severity"; Q4 "roll-forward testing only... finalize severity conclusions... management's 404(a) conclusion"

expectations.text: Places user access reviews quarterly and terminations/privileged-access checks as continuous — the classic late-surprise sources
expectations.evidence: UARs are placed quarterly (Q1-Q4), but terminations/privileged access are a "mid-year privileged/user access review" checkpoint — not continuous monitoring

expectations.text: Builds remediation timing logic: controls fixed late can't demonstrate sufficient operating history — deficiencies found in Q3 or earlier leave a re-test window; that's why triage belongs mid-year
expectations.evidence: "last chance to catch and fix an issue with enough runway to demonstrate the control operating effectively again before year-end"; "days to remediate" metric quantifies the re-test window

expectations.text: Includes deficiency aggregation and severity classification (AS 2201/Reg S-X ladder) ahead of the year-end conclusion, with audit-committee reporting for significant deficiencies
expectations.evidence: Severity classification and audit-committee presentation covered, but no AS 2201/Reg S-X ladder reference and no cross-deficiency aggregation analysis (only per-issue "trending toward" review)

expectations.text: References current context accurately where used: COSO 2013 as the framework, PCAOB inspection focus on ICFR, ~8% of recent annual reports disclosing material weaknesses with IT/access among top themes
expectations.evidence: Context used is accurate: "per PCAOB guidance on using interim testing with a roll-forward period"; annual SOC report review and CUEC mapping; no inaccurate framework or regulatory claims
